input.question: Which educational institution did Pablo Manzano Baena attend?

documents.text: As Pablo Manzano Baena strolled along the banks of the River Mersey, the Liver Building's imposing presence loomed before him, its clock tower piercing the grey Liverpool sky like a giant's fist. He had always been drawn to this city, with its rich history and irrepressible spirit. It was here, at the University of Liverpool, that he had spent some of the most formative years of his life, pouring over dusty tomes in the Harold Cohen Library and debating the intricacies of research methodology with his peers in the cramped, coffee-scented rooms of the Guild of Students. Pablo's mind wandered back to those heady days as he made his way to the university's Victoria Building, its Gothic Revival façade a testament to the institution's proud heritage. He was scheduled to meet with his former supervisor, Dr. Rachel Patel, to discuss a potential collaboration on a new project. As he climbed the worn stone steps, the sound of laughter and conversation drifted out of the foyer, transporting him back to a time when the world seemed full of endless possibility. Inside, the familiar scent of old books and fresh coffee enveloped him, and Pablo felt a sense of nostalgia wash over him. He spotted Rachel, her dark hair streaked with grey, chatting with a group of students in the corner of the foyer. Her eyes lit up as she caught sight of him, and she excused herself to greet him with a warm smile. "Pablo, it's been far too long!" she exclaimed, as they exchanged a brief, firm handshake. "I see you're still sporting that stylishly rumpled look. Some things never change, do they?" Pablo chuckled, feeling a sense of ease wash over him. "I try to maintain some consistency in my life, Rachel. But I have to say, it's great to be back in this place. It feels like coming home." As they made their way to Rachel's office, Pablo couldn't help but notice the subtle changes that had taken place since his time as a student. The university was still a hub of intellectual curiosity, but there was a newfound sense of purpose, a sense that the research being conducted here could have a real, tangible impact on the world. It was a feeling that resonated deeply with Pablo, and he knew that he was exactly where he was meant to be.
